stimuli.description: Two distinct light settings: 'warm, dim lighting' (CCT 2708 K, 97 lux on eye) and 'cool, bright lighting' (CCT 5854 K, 1021 lux on eye). These were used to create four experimental conditions: Warm Dim (no transition), Warm Dim to Cool Bright, Cool Bright (no transition), Cool Bright to Warm Dim.

tables.description: Participant descriptors including Body Mass Index, Midsleep (MSFsc), PSQI score, General Health (SF-36), Light Sensitivity (Eye Problems, Headache, Sunglasses), and Thermal Sensitivity.
a-opic irradiances of the warm, dim and cool, bright light settings for S-cone-opic, M-cone-opic, L-cone-opic, Rhodopic, and Melanopic.
Test statistics (Δ, T ratio, P value) of the main effect of light transition (WD to CB vs. Constant WD, and CB to WD vs. Constant CB) on various dependent variables.

limitations: CCT and illuminance were manipulated simultaneously, preventing attribution of effects to either alone.
Time of day effects on individual responsiveness to light could not be tested due to group sizes.
Abrupt transitions were used; results might differ with more gradual transitions.
Laboratory study (90 min duration); results need validation in longer field experiments and field settings.
Need for replication with participants from different cultural backgrounds.
